newsitem.title: GERMANY: IG Metall says prepared to discuss 97 wage demand.
newsitem.headline: IG Metall says prepared to discuss 97 wage demand.

text.p: German engineering union IG Metall chairman Klaus Zwickel said on Friday that his union was prepared to discuss its 1997 wage claim with employers if progress was made in a dispute over sick pay cuts.
"If an acceptable framework is reached in talks on sick pay, Christmas and holiday pay, it is not ruled out to find a suitable wage figure," Zwickel told a news conference.
That meant talks with employers on the 1997 wage claim could go ahead on Monday, Zwickel said. The talks would start on Monday in the town of Sulzbach near Frankfurt, an IG Metall spokesman said.
IG Metall indicated earlier this month it would be happy with a 1997 wage settlement of between 4.5 and five percent.
It said at the time that more than half of that increase could be used on measures designed to guarantee employment, effectively paving the way for a wage freeze in real terms.
